beats.role_note: The mechanism before the build — what synthetic lethality IS
beats.narration_text: Synthetic lethality: two genes, each dispensable alone, lethal when both are lost together. This plate shows the mechanism in two panels — two routes, two possible states. With one route cut, the other still reaches the survival node. With both cut, nothing gets through.

beats.role_note: Stakes before the build — BRCA×PARP mechanism
beats.narration_text: BRCA-mutated tumors use backup DNA repair because their primary repair pathway is already broken. PARP inhibitors cut the backup. The tumor had one route already severed — adding the second cut is synthetic lethality in action. Normal cells with intact BRCA survive; BRCA-mutant tumor cells don't.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL B05_SyntheticLethality class, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it. The panel function takes two arguments: y-centre and a boolean for whether both routes are cut. Each panel draws a start circle, two polyline routes through bent mid-points, an X-mark on the upper route, and either a GREEN circle or an ORANGE broken polygon as the survival node. Two calls, two panels, one separator line. The choreography is top-panel then bottom-panel — building the contrast deliberately.

props.title: scenes.py — B05_SyntheticLethality
props.code:
# Synthetic lethality — two panels, two routes, two states
GRAY="#7c7c7c"; VERM="#D55E00"; GREEN="#009E73"; ORANGE="#E69F00"

def panel(cy, both):
    start=Circle(radius=0.32,color=GRAY,fill_color=GRAY,fill_opacity=0.35).move_to([-5,cy,0])
    up=[[-5,cy,0],[-1.5,cy+1.4,0],[1.5,cy+1.4,0],[4.5,cy,0]]
    lo=[[-5,cy,0],[-1.5,cy-1.4,0],[1.5,cy-1.4,0],[4.5,cy,0]]
    up_poly=VMobject(stroke_color=GRAY,stroke_width=3); up_poly.set_points_as_corners(up)
    lo_poly=VMobject(stroke_color=GRAY,stroke_width=3); lo_poly.set_points_as_corners(lo)
    xm=_xmark(-0.0,cy+1.4)
    if both:
        xm2=_xmark(-0.0,cy-1.4)
        surv=_broken_node(4.5,cy)
        return start,up_poly,lo_poly,xm,xm2,surv
    surv=Circle(radius=0.38,color=GREEN,fill_color=GREEN,fill_opacity=0.3).move_to([4.5,cy,0])
    return start,up_poly,lo_poly,xm,surv

class B05_SyntheticLethality(Scene):
  def construct(self):
    sep=Line([-7,0,0],[7,0,0],color=GRAY,stroke_width=1.5)
    self.play(Create(sep))
    self.play(*[FadeIn(m) for m in panel(1.8,False)])
    self.play(*[FadeIn(m) for m in panel(-1.8,True)])

beats.role_note: Manim render of B05_SyntheticLethality — top panel then bottom panel
beats.narration_text: Run it. Separator line first — two spaces, two fates. Top panel: start circle, both routes draw, X-mark on the upper route, GREEN survival node intact. Bottom panel: same start, same routes, X-marks on both — ORANGE broken node. The visual contrast is the argument: one cut, you survive. Two cuts, no route remains.

beats.narration_text: The change. Revise: build the top panel first — one cut survives. Then the second route's X-mark appears with a large VERM Flash. The GREEN survival node suddenly shatters — replace it with the ORANGE broken polygon using ReplacementTransform. Add a slight Wiggle on the broken node. Show the second cut as the lethal event.

beats.role_note: Manim render of B07_SyntheticLethalityBreak — Flash X2, shatter, Wiggle
beats.narration_text: Watch the revision. Top panel builds — one route cut, GREEN node intact. Then the second X-mark fires: a large VERM Flash. The GREEN node shatters into the ORANGE broken polygon — ReplacementTransform, instant. A brief Wiggle on the broken node punches the lethality. The second cut is the drug. The motion makes the BRCA × PARP argument without a single word of explanation.

beats.role_note: What we built and what the motion taught
beats.narration_text: Redundancy is safety until it isn't. The motion made the geometry physical: one cut survives because the other route compensates. Both cut and there's nowhere to go. The second X-mark is the drug. Claude ported the two-panel plate in one prompt and added the shatter event in one revision. The pattern: build the redundancy, show the first cut, detonate the second. Strip that and you can animate any synthetic lethality pair.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud AND discussed. greeting = 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt into Claude: add a third panel below the two — a NORMAL CELL where both routes are intact, both reach a GREEN node. Animate all three panels top to bottom, and label the result of each one: survive, survive, die. Why run it? Because the therapeutic window argument depends on that third panel. Olaparib kills BRCA-mutant cells because the first route was already severed. Normal cells have both routes intact and tolerate PARP inhibition. The three-panel version makes the selectivity argument complete — you can see exactly why the drug is not just a poison.
